data.title: Route Overview
paragraphs: This itinerary treats Georgia and Armenia as neighbouring cultures with distinct voices rather than flattening them into a single “Caucasus” aesthetic. Tbilisi and Kakheti begin with wine, food, and urban history before the road climbs toward Kazbegi.

After crossing into Armenia, Yerevan provides a new architectural and culinary rhythm, followed by monastery landscapes around Geghard, Dilijan, and Lake Sevan. The route privileges family tables, small producers, and stone architecture over checklist touring.
highlights: Tbilisi neighbourhoods and contemporary Georgian food culture.
Kakheti qvevri wine traditions and family-scale cellar visits.
Kazbegi mountain landscapes and village roads.
Armenian monastery architecture around Geghard, Dilijan, and Sevan.

introParagraphs: This 12-day journey is paced around wine, monasteries & mountains, realistic transfers, and enough time in each region for the place to develop beyond first impressions.

data.title: BORDER & WINE NOTE
data.text: Cross-border procedures and transport arrangements can change, so the exact Georgia–Armenia connection should be reconfirmed before travel. Wine transport limits should also be checked for the traveller’s onward destination.

data.title: Two Countries, One Long Conversation
paragraphs: Georgia and Armenia share mountain geography and ancient Christian traditions, yet their architecture, wine, bread, music, and urban life remain wonderfully distinct.
The route works because it gives each country enough time to speak before drawing connections between them.

items.question: Can Wine Roads & Stone Monasteries be tailored to our dates and interests?
paragraphs: Yes. Mariam Beridze’s route is a design framework rather than a fixed group departure. Stays, activity intensity, and specialist visits can be adjusted while protecting the geographic logic of the journey.
items.listTitle: Common ways to personalise the route:
listItems: Add or remove a night at the most important base.
Reduce walking or replace it with a lower-intensity alternative.
Add a specialist food, craft, wildlife, or photography focus where locally appropriate.

items.question: What is the best season for this journey?
paragraphs: Cross-border procedures and transport arrangements can change, so the exact Georgia–Armenia connection should be reconfirmed before travel. Wine transport limits should also be checked for the traveller’s onward destination.

items.question: What is included in the estimated journey budget?
listItems: Handpicked accommodation described in the final confirmed proposal.
Private or pre-arranged ground transfers listed in the route.
Specialist guiding and scheduled cultural or nature experiences.
On-ground coordination for the confirmed itinerary.

items.question: How physically demanding is the itinerary?
paragraphs: The default pace is described as generous. Walking, altitude, wildlife activity, or outdoor intensity varies by region, so the final version should be adjusted to the traveller’s fitness, health, and comfort.
listItems: Alternative or shorter activity options are used where practical.
Weather and local conditions can change the day plan.

items.question: How far in advance should we plan?
paragraphs: For small lodges, specialist guides, rail or ferry seats, light-aircraft sectors, or permit-sensitive experiences, planning several months ahead gives the best flexibility. The exact lead time depends on season and destination.

items.question: How are reservations confirmed and scheduled?
paragraphs: Once the final route, accommodation, and specialist experiences are approved, a 30% confirmation deposit is used to secure services. The remaining balance is normally due 45 days before arrival unless a supplier requires different terms.

items.question: What is the policy for date changes or cancellations?
paragraphs: We try to shift dates or restructure the route whenever suppliers allow, but remote lodges, permits, flights, ferries, and specialist appointments may carry their own non-refundable conditions.
listItems: 60+ days before arrival: refund or credit is calculated after non-refundable supplier costs.
30–59 days before arrival: partial refund or rescheduling credit depends on confirmed supplier terms.
Less than 30 days before arrival: cancellation follows the individual confirmed service conditions.
